correctness.rationale: Strong-Markov nearest-site regeneration gives iid symmetric independent jump directions and times; a matching backward boundary problem derives the source Laplace transform. Explicit endpoint asymptotics and dimensional factors were verified. The source and 223 checker assertions corroborate but do not substitute for infinite arguments.

originality.rationale: The published nearest-site model provides the inter-neighbor first-passage Laplace transform and diffusion optimum, not the strict all-rate 2/3<CV^2<1 renewal-variability window or exact globally positive displacement fourth-cumulant law. The general fixed-site reset renewal-pole literature supplies methodology, not the present object-specific inequality. Three targeted current research-record queries, four alternate-name web searches, and inspection of the original and published source PDFs found no direct stronger claim. The mathematical novelty is the global sign, not the established transform or the generic renewal expansion; residual priority risk remains.
residual_risks: General semi-Markov random-walk renewal theorems may implicitly entail the two-thirds sign threshold; here the claim of novelty is restricted to proving strict all-rate 2/3<CV^2<1 for this precise nearest-site physical model.

value.rationale: The 2024 nearest-site reset literature studies enhancement and optimization of effective diffusivity. The new strict 2/3-to-1 waiting-time fluctuation window yields a parameter-independent positive long-time fourth-cumulant signature across enhanced and suppressed diffusion, including the optimum, and isolates a direct measurable non-Gaussian transport prediction. The inequality is not a textbook normalization calculation, requiring a global hyperbolic-series positivity result. Boundaries and limitations are explicit.
